Plot a co-occurrence network

Source: R/methods.R
plot.cooccurrence.Rd

plot() draws one of three displays of a co-occurrence network: a heatmap of the weight matrix (default), a network drawing through igraph, or the degree distribution as a bar chart. The heatmap shows which item pairs carry the heaviest weights and which never co-occur. The network drawing places linked items near one another. The degree distribution shows whether connectivity is concentrated on a few hub items or spread evenly.

The heatmap uses a white-to-blue scale for non-negative weights and a red-white-blue scale centered on zero when weights can be negative (scale = "zscore"); rows are the source items, which matters for the directed similarity = "relative" network.

For a result built with split_by, group names the network to draw. For publication-quality network drawings, convert with as_cograph() and use cograph::splot().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'cooccurrence'
plot(x, type = c("heatmap", "network", "degree"), group = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

A cooccurrence edge list from cooccurrence().

type

"heatmap" (default), "network" (requires igraph), or "degree".

group

For a result built with split_by, the name of the group to draw. NULL (default) for an unsplit result.

...

Passed to graphics::image() for the heatmap, plot() on the igraph object for the network, and graphics::barplot() for the degree distribution, where they override the defaults (for instance col or main).

Value

x, invisibly and unchanged. Called for the plot drawn on the current graphics device.

Conditions

cooccure_grouped_input when x was built with split_by and group is NULL; cooccure_missing_package for type = "network" without igraph.

See also

as_cograph() for publication network drawings; summary.cooccurrence() for the numbers behind the degree plot.

Examples

net <- cooccurrence(movies, field = "genres", sep = ",",
                    similarity = "jaccard", min_occur = 50)
plot(net)

plot(net, type = "degree")
